text.tspan: Everyday English - C2 - 2026/11/18 - Essay - 01
A musician holds a guitar.
Pexels · 18390140
Listening without distraction
To listen to a whole album is to negotiate a familiar but frequently obscured relationship between intentional design and the contingencies of shared
experience. The question is not whether arrangements are desirable, but what authority they should acquire. A credible position supports preparation while
withholding the assumption that procedural coherence is equivalent to human value.
There is a substantive case for structure: setting aside distractions lets us notice more of the music. Here, we put the phone away during the first song.
The arrangement earns its legitimacy through the specific difficulty it alleviates, not through its conformity to an abstract ideal of order. Its success is
consequently conditional. Once the intervention demands more attention than the obstacle it removes, the original justification begins to unravel.
An assessment confined to that practical benefit would nevertheless be incomplete, since sharing different preferences makes listening more interesting.
In concrete terms, each friend chooses one track and explains what they enjoy about it. This introduces a problem of perspective: whose convenience
supplies the standard against which improvement is measured? An apparently neutral procedure may privilege the preferences of its designer.
Attentiveness to others makes that asymmetry visible and creates grounds for revision.
What emerges is a qualified defence of planning, rather than a celebration of either control or spontaneity. Arrangements can sustain an experience
without exhausting its meaning. Their authority should remain answerable to the people and circumstances they affect; otherwise, a means of making life
more habitable risks becoming the criterion to which life must conform.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each body paragraph
needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Write guidance for someone who wants to listen to a whole album for the first time. Explain two useful choices and why they matter. Use four short
paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss setting aside distractions
lets us notice more of the music with an example; discuss sharing different preferences makes listening more interesting with a different example;
conclude by connecting the two points.)
